entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hasan Ali, also known as Sultan Hasanali or Hasanali Beg, was the last sultan of the Qara Qoyunlu state and the son of Jahan Shah Haqİqi. Born into a prominent family, he was groomed for leadership from an early age. In 1467, after the assassination of his father, Hasanali attempted to restore Qara Qoyunlu rule in the south of Azerbaijan, but was killed in 1469 before achieving this goal.

The Qara Qoyunlu state was a powerful khanate that played a significant role in the regional politics of the Middle East during the 15th century. Its rise and fall had a profound impact on the history of Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkey.

Hasanali's efforts to restore Qara Qoyunlu rule were part of a broader struggle for regional power and influence. His legacy continues to be felt in the modern-day politics of the Caucasus region.

The death of Hasanali in 1469 marked the end of an era for the Qara Qoyunlu state, which was eventually absorbed into the Ottoman Empire. However, his memory lives on as a symbol of regional pride and resistance to foreign domination.
